A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RSV is a very potent inducer of cell mediated immune response.
RSV induces natural killer (NK) cells in the respiratory tract of cotton rat and that these NK cells are cytotoxic for RSV-infected cells.
RSV infection induces a significant cytotoxic activity in splenic and respiratory tract mononuclear cells which may play an important role in the elimination of virus-infected cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RSV infection of the respiratory tract induces a significant cytotoxic activity in pulmonary mononuclear cells and in the spleen.
the respiratory tract is a very important immune organ.
there is a strong correlation between the induction of cytotoxicity and viral replication at the site of infection.
